messages:
maria: opening this thread to capture follow-up from the late-night 503 spike affecting streaming endpoints. customers reported 5xx + timeouts; support escalated. placing notes and action items here. :warning:

sam: quick summary from logs — burst of 503s aligned with auth-service 429->retry cascade, billing KMS started returning transient errors at ~02:14 UTC, caused token refreshes to backpressure gateway. big fanout from streaming sessions (~x3 normal).

jordan: repro snippet i used to simulate the burst (local):

```bash
for i in $(seq 1 200); do 
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream -H 'Authorization: Bearer TEST' -d '{"input":"hello"}' &
done
wait
```

that produced ~12% 503s locally with our staging auth proxy pointed at the flaky billing-kms stub.

lee: notes on root cause: billing KMS had a maintenance windows and we had no circuit around the token refresh path. when KMS returned 5xx/429 the auth proxy retried aggressively, filling connection pools on apigw and downstream runtime -> streaming keepalives started timing out.

maria: timeline we think: 02:12 UTC billing KMS maintenance kicked, 02:14 auth proxy retries spike, 02:15 gateway connpool exhaustion, 02:16 first customer reports, 02:25 mitigations gradually restored.

sam: short-term mitigations we applied during the incident: reduced auth retry count to 1, enabled short-lived token caching at gateway (~30s) for streaming sessions, temporarily increased gateway max conns by 20% to absorb burst. these dropped 503s to <0.5% by 02:28.

jordan: reproduction steps for a support runbook: 1) point auth proxy at KMS stub that returns 429 in spikes; 2) run the curl fanout; 3) observe gateway 503s + streaming timeouts. I can write the stub harness.

lee: long-term fixes proposed: 1) add circuit breaker on auth->KMS (open after N failures per minute), 2) make token refresh backoff jittered + exponential with capped concurrency, 3) add pre-warmed token cache per-session to avoid per-request refresh in streaming flows, 4) improve observability (per-token TTL metrics + k8s restart telemetry).

maria: action items & owners:
- jordan: publish repro harness + instructions in /incidents (ETA: tomorrow 10:00 PT)
- sam: implement auth proxy circuit breaker and reduced retry logic (ETA: 3 working days)
- lee: design token cache for streaming sessions, spec + rollout plan (ETA: 1 week)
- support: draft customer comms and update affected accounts list (ETA: today EOD)
- maria: run a postmortem doc + link to alerts and dashboards (ETA: 2 days)

support: i'm compiling impacted customer list now. initial set: 4 enterprise accounts saw elevated errors, two reported revenue-impacting failures — i'll surface those for priority comms.

maria: risk/rollback plan for auth changes — we'll canary circuit breaker in eu-west first and keep an automatic fallback to current behavior for hosts in case of regressions. keep ops-sre looped.

sam: quick note — we should also evaluate billing KMS SLA and add monitoring alert for sustained 5xx/429 > 30s, currently only p95 latency is alerted.

jordan: added a small example to the repro harness to assert that streaming keepalive resets spike when auth fails; will attach logs and minimal k6 script.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: auth-proxy/retry-limiter v1.2.4 -> canary eu-west (by sam)

sam: starting canary now, will watch 5xx rate and connpool metrics for next 30m. ping if you see regressions.

lee: question — do we want to also add a transient fallback model route for streaming (lower-cost, lower-throughput model) when gateway latency crosses threshold? could reduce end-user impact while root cause is fixed.

maria: yes, include fallback routing as a runbook item but not blocking the auth fixes. sam/lee include cost/ops impact in your specs.

support: customer comms draft ready — short explanation + mitigation + ask for any affected logs. posting to #customers in 10m for approvals.

maria: good summary. we'll reconvene after sam's canary and jordan's harness is published. closing this thread for new actions; update this thread with links to PRs, canary logs, and the final postmortem doc. :white_check_mark:
